_comment: THE FIRST REAL FRAGMENT of the Book layer (Capa de Libro), and the
format documentation: this file shows every field a fragment has.
It used to be documented by a separate sample file whose name began
with an underscore. Godot treats a file whose name starts with '_' as
hidden, so it was never in the FileSystem, FileAccess could not open
it, and no tool could check it - and it carried the 1615 wording under
an 'original_1605' key, which is exactly the mistake rule 3 exists to
catch. A worked example that teaches the error and cannot be read is
worse than no example, so the format lives here, where the validator
can see it.
THE FIELDS:
id                the fragment's id: bk.ch<chapter>.<slug>.<index>
chapter           the chapter of the novel the passage is from
part              the part of the novel (1 or 2)
title_key         the locale key for the fragment's title
characters        who is in the passage
source            where it came from: work, edition, url,
public_domain, verified, verified_on
original_1605     THE 1605 WORDING, VERBATIM. Content: the same in
every build, in every language. Never a key.
modern            one modernized rendering per language
pd_translations   optional: a public-domain translation per language
variants          the Reality and the Book reading of the passage
unlocks           what the passage gives: codex_page, recuerdos_bonus
RULES:
1. Source every fragment from a public-domain edition:
- Wikisource (es.wikisource.org/wiki/Don_Quijote)
- Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes
- Project Gutenberg (for PD translations)
2. Always record the provenance in the 'source' block.
3. Set 'verified' to true only after a human checked it against the
edition. Unverified fragments must not ship.
4. If a PD translation of this passage exists in the player's
language (Motteux 1700 / Ormsby 1901 / Florian 1799 / etc.),
it goes in 'pd_translations' and the UI offers it as a third tab.
5. The 'modern' rendering must keep the RHYTHM and the strangeness.
A modernised Don Quixote is a different, and worse, book.
!! THE 1605 / 1615 DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING !!
DLC 1 is 'El Segundo Libro (1615)': the book the world keeps rewriting
itself into. So which edition a fragment comes from is not a detail.
The 1605 incipit reads:
'...de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocin flaco y
galgo corredor.'
The 1615 revision replaces that with:
'...de los de lanza en astillero, galera en coraza y bacia en el
casco.'
The line has to be checked against the 1605 printing, not against a
modern edition that happens to be more available. The validator
flags any fragment that carries the 1615 wording, and the test suite
fails the build if a fragment the game reads has not been verified.
This fragment was checked against the 1605 text quoted by Wikisource
on 19 October 2026, and it is the 1605 wording.

source.work: Miguel de Cervantes, El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quijote de la Mancha, parte I, cap. I
source.verified_note: The 1605 incipit was checked against the text Wikisource quotes from the 1605 edition ('adarga antigua, rocin flaco y galgo corredor'). A human should still read it against a facsimile before the fragment ships in a build.

original_1605: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no ha mucho tiempo que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocín flaco y galgo corredor.

modern.es: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no hace mucho que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocín flaco y galgo corredor.
modern.es_419: En un lugar de la Mancha, del que prefiero no acordarme, no hace mucho que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocín flaco y galgo corredor.
modern.en: In a place in La Mancha, whose name I do not care to recall, there lived not long ago one of those gentlemen who are accustomed to a lance in the rack, an old sword, a lean nag and a greyhound.
modern.fr: En un lieu de la Manche, dont je ne veux pas me souvenir du nom, vivait naguère un gentilhomme de ceux qui portent lance au râtelier, une vieille épée, un cheval maigre et un lévrier gris.

en.text: In a place in La Mancha, whose name I have no mind to remember, there dwelt not long since one of those gentlemen that are commonly called knights of the lance and buckler...

fr.text: En un lieu de la Manche, dont je ne veux pas me souvenir le nom, vivoit nagueres un gentilhomme de ceux qui portent lance au ratelier...

variants.reality: La realidad: the plain is empty. The mill is a mill. (No text is shown; the scene speaks.)
variants.book: El libro: the mill is a giant. (The text is shown, with the Book layer's typography.)
